# MVT Games - llms.txt

> MVT (Model-View-Ticker) is an architecture for frame-based interactive
> applications. This file provides a compressed entry point for LLMs.

## Architecture

MVT splits applications into three layers:

- **Model** - owns state and domain logic. Advances only via update(deltaMs).
  No wall-clock time, no view references, no presentation values.
- **View** - reads state, writes presentation output. Stateless (no domain
  state). refresh() runs each frame, must be idempotent and side-effect free.
- **Ticker** - drives the loop each frame: model.update(deltaMs) then
  view.update(deltaMs) (views with state) then view.refresh() then render.
  One turn is a tick: the ticker ticks the models, then the views. In this
  repo, views set update and refresh methods on their Pixi containers with
  setUpdate(view, update) and setRefresh(view, refresh), and the host calls
  updateView(app.stage, deltaMs) and then refreshView(app.stage) (from
  @mvtjs/pixi) once per frame, after the models: updateView calls every
  update method in the stage, then refreshView every refresh method, parents
  first. Views never forward these calls by hand.
- **Bindings** - contract between view and model. Query bindings read state
  (a function called each frame, or a fixed value read once); relay bindings
  report user input out of the view. In this repo, query bindings are named
  for what they return (score, isAlive) and relay bindings are on*() members.
  Reusable views take query and relay bindings; a top-level view's binding
  is the model itself, a fixed value.

## Frame Sequence

Every frame: compute deltaMs, cap it, update models, advance view
presentation state, refresh views, render. Models settle before views read.

## Key Rules

- Models: all state through update(deltaMs) only. No setTimeout, Date.now(),
  auto-playing tweens. Domain-level coordinates (tiles, world-units), not
  pixels. Parent delegates update() to children.
- Views: no domain state. refresh() is idempotent, read-only. Re-read
  every changing value every frame (never cache it at construction); only a
  query binding declared as a fixed value may be read once. May hold cosmetic
  presentation state (gains update(deltaMs), set with setUpdate). Extract complex presentation
  logic to a view model.
- Ticker: strict sequence (update models, update views, refresh views,
  render). Cap deltaMs. No domain
  logic or rendering code.
- Hot paths: no per-tick allocations. Index-based for loops. Pre-allocated
  structures. Change detection for expensive infrequent rebuilds.

## Project Conventions (this repo only)

- Factory functions, not classes: createXxxModel(options) -> XxxModel
- Views are functions: XxxView(bindings: XxxViewBindings), returning a
  Pixi container, three.js object or DOM element, usable as a JSX tag or
  a plain call. A top-level view takes { model }. The body may be JSX or plain
  TypeScript, whichever suits the view; neither is required. JSX tends to
  suit trees of display objects that follow the model, plain TypeScript views
  that mostly draw or manage their own display objects.
- Barrel imports only: never import past index.ts
- Sound is a view's job. An audio view plays sounds instead of drawing
  visuals. It calls reactions (createReaction) in its refresh step, and
  plays on a change, never on a state alone. A phase that begins is a
  change, and so is a count that rises (shotsFired, with when: increased).
  A sound for the state it starts in is played as the view is made. Audio
  views play on sound chips from audio90, the Audio80 (4 mono voices)
  or the Audio90 (16 stereo voices of FM, analog and samples). An entry
  names its kind of chip in its starter and gets two: music, for its
  songs, and sfx, for its sound effects. Repeating sounds, such as a
  heartbeat, are presentation state, advanced in the update step. Music
  plays on the chip's own sequencer, on the sound card's clock, so a late
  frame never holds it up: a view only chooses which song plays and how
  fast, with the music chip's play, queue, stop and tempoScale. The chips
  keep the sound card's time, so the entry host pauses them as it pauses
  the game.
- String-literal unions, not enums
- 4-space indent, lower-kebab-case files, PascalCase types, camelCase rest
- A file is named for its main export, whatever folder it is in
  (bounceAudio90Song in bounce-audio90-song.ts, createScoreModel in
  score-model.ts)
- TypeScript 5.9, Pixi.js 8, GSAP 3, Vite 8

## Documentation

- packages/sites/docs/index.md - the preface to the book, Building Web
  Games with MVT
- packages/sites/docs/chapters/ - the book's chapters, one per file in
  reading order (01-games-in-the-browser.md to 34-using-the-principles.md), with a
  chapter for each of the eight design principles (SoC, SSOT, CQS, DIP,
  CRP, DbC, MISU, DfT) in Part VII
- packages/sites/docs/appendices/ - the rules on one page (A), the glossary
  (B), measurements and benchmarking (C, D), GSAP timelines (E),
  troubleshooting (F), the API cheat sheets (G), and MVT beyond the
  web (H)
- packages/sites/docs/working-in-this-repo/ - code style, project structure,
  and the writing guide
- packages/sites/docs/ai-agents/ - task-specific skills files for agents
  (not published), which link into the book
- packages/libraries/audio90/docs/ - guides to the Audio80 and Audio90 sound chips and their tracker music
- AGENTS.md - compressed agent entry point (canonical)
